detail: Algebra checked: canonical col 0 is u0(x)v1 with u0=1/sqrt(na) (rho=0.4>0 gives lam0/lam1=3.67 (B4x12) and 6.33 (B8x52), no tie), so the loading is exactly date-constant (max deviation 0.0 in both cases) and all vdate>0 (min 0.0256 / 0.0056). With date-constant v the log-form barrier equation is linear in z, so Stage C 8-step Newton is exact after one step and the closed form equals it; the strike root uses the same start (abar, vbar = means over dim), and by Jensen g(z0)>=0 with g convex increasing, so Newton decreases monotonically to the root (no divergence; 60 vs 8 iterations is immaterial at tested points). Grouped CDF sum is an exact regrouping. zh<=zs gives hi=lo and h=0 identically in both kernels. Independent test on fresh points (2^14 N(0,1); 2^12 each of U[-6,6], 2.5*N clipped at 6, ndtri of extreme tails to 1e-15; a 15,424-point sign-aligned sweep across the knock-out transition) gives max |fast - StageC| <= 9.5e-13 and zero mismatches in the h=0 set; an adaptive-quadrature brute force of E[f|y] on 387 points (35 with 0<zh-zs<0.01) agrees to 1.5e-13.
evidence: scratchpad review_c10/agree.py and agree.json (B8x52 normal_2^14 max_abs 1.3e-13; sweep 9.5e-13; brute 1.5e-13; B4x12 similar).
suggested_fix: Cosmetic: selfcheck reports max relative diff on 4,096 Sobol points only; relative diff on tiny positive h at extreme points reaches 8e-8 (absolute 1e-13), so quote absolute agreement (<=1e-12) rather than 6e-13 relative, and note the rho>0 / no-tie precondition for date-constant loading.

detail: AS241 (PPND16) coefficients and branch points (|q|<=0.425, r<=5) match Wichura 1988; clipping bounds identical to the Stage C np.clip(1e-15, 1-1e-15). Against scipy.special.ndtri: 4.19M uniforms max abs 2.7e-15, max rel 1.2e-15 (|z|>1e-3), abs 6.5e-19 near zero; 1.05M log-uniform lower-tail points in (1e-15, 0.1) and their 1-p mirrors max rel 8.7e-16; branch boundaries and the 1e-15 clip exact to 3.7e-16. Against 40-digit mpmath on 2,000 points: AS241 max rel 4.9e-16, scipy 5.0e-16. Upper tail loses the same precision in 1-p for both (identical input rounding), so the normals, hence the estimator, are unchanged to ~1e-15.

Protocol vs item C2 is fair: same n_run (2^17/2^17/2^11/2^12), 16 workers x 16 scrambles, all-16 wall from submission to mean+hw, factor rebuilt per run inside the interval, warm pool, identical seed keys across methods, order rotated, idle check per cell, 20 reps (minor: no prefix-mark cumsum as in C2, negligible). The problem is the transfer 'primary T_C = 1 Oct primary / paired speedup'. (a) The ratio is demonstrably state-dependent: same-day B8x52 $0.001 measurements give Stage C 11.09 s (paired run) vs 10.26 s (unchanged C2 harness, c2_harness_today) vs 10.28 s (h16_fast 16-worker leg, same rt.all16 code), with the fast leg stable at 4.94-4.95 s; so the same-day 16-worker speedup is 2.25 (paired) or 2.08 (two independent runs). At 1 worker it is 2.49 (h16_fast), single-process profile ~2.5. The Oct1-to-today Stage C factor itself varies by cell (2.03, 2.33, 2.35, 2.74), i.e. the state change is not a uniform clock scaling (hybrid Meteor Lake 155H, 16 workers on 6P+8E+2LPE: the all-16 wall is set by the slowest core class), so the fast/StageC ratio in the 1 Oct state is unknown to about +/-15% in either direction. (b) Spec 0.5 says an uncertain choice takes the QF option as primary (larger T_C); 2.25 is the CF end of the same-day evidence. With 2.08: T_C = 10.84 s, window M = 21.4, all-free 1.06, symmetric (C09) 0.633. The 'all-free floor no longer reaches M<=1' statement flips if the reference-state speedup is < 1.96 (13% below 2.25), within the observed state dependence. (c) Attributing the 2.2x machine difference to the Best-performance overlay is unverified (the 1 Oct overlay is unknown).
evidence: results/c10_challengers_20261022/timing/run001/c10_timing.json (per-rep ratios 2.195-2.383; Stage C walls 10.91-11.83); c2_harness_today/run001.json walls 10.21-10.88 (median 10.26); h16_fast/run001/h16_fast.json w16 preint 10.283 / fast 4.946 = 2.079, w1 ratio 2.487; results/frontier_classical_20261001/c2/c2_timing.json B8x52 preint 0.001 median 22.53 (scale 1.0).
suggested_fix: Identify the reference state empirically: re-run c2_harness_today under each power-mode overlay until one reproduces ~22.5 s (the user must switch the overlay), then run the 20-rep paired timing there. Until then report T_C as a bracket 22.53/{2.25, 2.08} = 10.0-10.8 s. Take the QF end as primary per spec 0.5 (10.84 s, harness-anchored: 22.53 x fast_today / c2_harness_today) and label 10.03 s CF. State the all-free floor as 1.06-1.15, which is not robustly > 1.

detail: Bound: Maurer & Pontil 2009 Thm 4 (one-sided) is sqrt(2 V_n ln(2/d)/n) + 7 ln(2/d)/(3(n-1)) for X in [0,1], with V_n the unbiased (ddof=1) sample variance. Scaling to [0,R] and a union bound over the two sides gives exactly the coded sqrt(2V ln(4/d)/n) + 7R ln(4/d)/(3(n-1)). var = (s2 - n mean^2)/(n-1) is ddof=1; cancellation is harmless at n=8e7, sd 1.15, mean 3.28. Range: the P1 argument (for z<z_H every date basket is <= H e^{-v_j(z_H-z)}, so h(y) <= h*(z_H(y))) is sound for the date-constant positive PCA loading, and h>=0 analytically. P1's hstar_max is a 0.01-step grid maximum on [-3,5), not a sup. Refining gives sup h* = 17.290078 (B8x52, at z_H=0.8424) and 15.862932 (B4x12), both < 17.30, and h* decays at the grid edges, so R=17.30 is valid (margin 0.0099). R is loose, but the R-term is only 3e-6 of the 4.455e-4 bound. Using 17.30 for B4x12 is valid (conservative). Fixed n from an independent pilot (purpose 12 vs 13, separate seed keys) is valid for a fixed-n bound: conditional on the pilot, n is deterministic. The bound is reported regardless of its value, so there is no optional stopping. Minor protocol point: the binding-cell C09 run started at 14.7% CPU, which is not idle under the D6 <10% rule. c09_g4.py logs machine_state but does not enforce it.
evidence: research/c10_challengers_20261022/c09_g4.py eb_bound/iid_run; scratchpad review_c10/hstar.py (refined sup 17.290078 / 15.862932); c09/B8x52_0.001_run001/c09_g4.json machine[0].cpu_percent_30s=14.65, n=80,419,536, bound 4.4553e-4, max h 8.58.
suggested_fix: Quote the refined sup (17.2901) instead of the grid value; enforce wait_idle in c09_g4.py or disclose the 14.7% start load.

detail: The object has the right shape (T_C,sym = T_C x F, hence M_sym = M/F, with numerator and denominator in the same state). But F = 33.8 is the cost of one distribution-free estimator (iid preint + MP EB), not the cheapest. The spec takes T_C as the minimum over validated estimators (0.3), so the symmetric analogue should be a minimum over distribution-free estimators; a faster one is q-. Counter-example (mod, no timing): replicated RQMC, i.e. m iid replicates, each the mean of n_r scrambled-Sobol preint values (still in [0,R]), with the same two-sided MP EB on the m means. Measured replicate sd on B8x52 (1,024 replicates each) gives a total point count of N/N_iid = 0.46 (n_r=8), 0.33 (16), 0.44 (32), 0.68 (64) and 1.22 (128). At n_r=16 that is 2.6e7 points instead of 7.9e7, about 3x fewer. scipy LMS costs 13 ms per d=416 replicate, so a cheap randomisation is needed: nested scrambling of only the 4 bits 16 points use, or random-shift lattices. With that, per-point cost is close to iid. Betting CIs (Waudby-Smith & Ramdas) shave roughly another 10%. If F falls to ~11-15, window symmetric M becomes ~1.5-2.1 instead of 0.684, and 'the symmetric convention is the only single departure reaching M<=1' would not hold. F is also measured in today's CF state and applied to the 1 Oct T_C, the same state-invariance assumption as in check 3.
evidence: scratchpad review_c10/df_rep.py output: n_r=16 sd(mean)=0.1092 (variance gain 6.9 over iid), m=1.60e6, N=2.56e7 vs iid EB 7.88e7; c09 B8x52 sigma_h 1.146.
suggested_fix: Label 33.8 as the 'iid-EB factor', a QF upper bound on the symmetric factor. Implement and time a replicated-RQMC EB estimator with cheap randomisation (n_r ~ 16), optionally with a betting CI, and report window symmetric M as a range until then.

detail: rate_cv supports the conclusion: sd ratio 0.96-1.03 across 2^6..2^18 for both cases, with unchanged fitted rates and n(0.001). Closed-form control means agree with the RQMC means to about 1-2 se (B8x52 controls 1 and 3 at 2.1 se; with beta ~20 that is a ~1e-6 effect, irrelevant). A possible hidden-gain bug is the iid-style pilot beta in place of an RQMC-optimal beta (Hickernell-Lemieux-Owen 2005). Tested with 64 scrambles, beta fitted on scramble means, leave-one-out, at n=2^10/2^12/2^14: residual sd ratios are 0.94-0.97 (no gain) and corr(h-mean, g-mean) <= 0.18. The controls' RQMC errors (sd 2e-5 at 2^14) are 80x smaller than h's and nearly uncorrelated with them. The negative is robust.
evidence: results/c10_challengers_20261022/rate_cv/run001/rate_cv.json sd_ratio; scratchpad review_c10/cv_rqmc_beta.py output (B8x52 ratio 0.949/0.969/0.957; B4x12 0.942/0.943/0.958).
suggested_fix: None for the RQMC negative. Separate note: controls cut the iid sd by 1.8x, which matters for the iid distribution-free route (C09). Only the geometric knock-out control is bounded, so the EB range term would need care.

detail: The sd ratios reproduce from the JSON: B8x52 k=8 gives 1.93 (Q6) and 2.03 (Q12) at 2^16, and 1.65-1.69 at 2^14. The k=1 negative holds. Two errors, both favouring the kill. (i) The break-even '6.64 x 1.93^(-1/0.6) = 2.2x longer' applies the kernel-only cost ratio to the whole pipeline. Sobol, ndtri and GEMM (~50 of ~66 ms per chunk in the fast pipeline, more under 16-worker contention) are not multiplied by Q. In whole-pipeline terms Q6 costs ~2.3x and Q12 ~3.9x, so equal accuracy takes ~0.77x (Q6) and ~1.2x (Q12) the preint time, not 2.2x. (ii) 'Q=12 agrees with h' is not supported. Against Q=48 on the same 2^14 points the quadrature bias is: Q6 -1.68e-3, Q8 -5.6e-4, Q10 +1.4e-4 (+/-1.0e-4), Q12 +2.7e-4 (+/-0.85e-4, 0.27 eps), Q16 +1.0e-4, Q20 +2e-5. Bias below ~0.1 eps needs Q>=16, which is ~1.3-1.5x slower than preint in whole-pipeline terms. So the kill holds for this implementation, but only by ~1.3x. A kernel that reuses exp(a) across nodes (exp(a + s w1) = exp(a) exp(node w1) exp(-z1 w1)) could reach break-even. Also, in B4x12 column 8 is an asset-dispersion mode; the second common time mode there is column 4, which was not tested (not binding).
evidence: rate_smooth2.json cost_ratio (kernel-only) and sd_ratio_top; selfcheck profile (kernel 15.5 of ~66 ms/chunk); scratchpad review_c10/smooth_bias.py output.
suggested_fix: Redo the break-even with whole-pipeline cost and an unbiased Q (>=16). State the kill as '~1.3-1.5x slower with this kernel; not robust to kernel optimisation'. Correct 'Q=12 agrees with h' to 'Q=12 bias ~0.27 eps'.

detail: The overrides apply only where intended. T_C is divided only when raw_best is preint and the key is one of the 4 measured cells (0.01 and 0.001, where envelope_applied is False, so env == best); OV_H16 and OV_DF replace only those 4 cells. The arithmetic follows: 10.2855 x 2.24623 = 23.1036; 23.1036/33.7772 = 0.6840; one-lane 23.1036/9.6213 = 2.4013; all-free 0.5107 x 2.2462 = 1.1471; all-free+symmetric 1.1471/33.777 = 0.0340; certified 801.48 x 2.2462 = 1800.3; explicit 231.96 x 2.2462 = 521.0. The U2-only and U1-only symmetric values (41.3/33.78 = 1.22; 30.2/33.78 = 0.894) are consistent. Bugs and inconsistencies: (i) the monotone envelope is computed before the override and not re-applied. B8x52|0.03 stays at 0.5535 s and B8x52|0.1 (oss) at 0.4137 s, both above the new B8x52|0.01 0.306 s; B4x12|0.03 stays at 0.1244 s, above B4x12|0.01 0.0583 s. Those cells' M is understated by 1.35-1.8x (QF). The binding minimum does not move, since fixing them only raises their M. (ii) Conventions are mixed: T_C transfers a same-day ratio to the 1 Oct state, but OV_H16 inserts today's absolute 1/16 ratio for the fast method (9.62). Transferred the same way it would be 10.24 x (9.62/11.51) = 8.56, giving one-lane M 2.70 instead of 2.40 (still a miss).
evidence: results/frontier_probe_20261021/headline/run004/headline_table.json T_C table and cells B8x52 0.001; run002 window primary 10.2855; overrides_run004.json; headline_m_probe.py lines 93-128 and 259-261.
suggested_fix: Apply the speedup before computing the envelope (or re-run the envelope after it). Use one convention for every state-dependent ratio: transfer, or re-baseline everything in today's state.

detail: Only partly established. The fast kernel is the Stage C estimand (pass), and the run004 arithmetic is correct given its inputs. Primary T_C 10.03 s depends on transferring a 2.25x ratio that two independent same-day runs put at 2.08x (T_C 10.84 s, window M 21.4, all-free 1.06), and the spec 0.5 QF rule would pick the smaller ratio. The measured factor 33.8 is valid for iid empirical Bernstein but is not the best distribution-free classical method: replicated RQMC with the same bound needs about 3x fewer points. So window symmetric M of 0.684 is a QF lower value, and M <= 1 under the symmetric convention is not established.
suggested_fix: Report T_C as 10.0-10.8 s (QF primary 10.84 s) until the reference state is reproduced; report symmetric M as a range with a replicated-RQMC distribution-free estimator; fix the envelope order in headline_m_probe.
